column3: The Hebrew has plural “his tents” for each man; BSB uses singular “his tent”.
The Hebrew says Judah’s men clung to their king; BSB has “stayed by”.
The Hebrew repeatedly calls the residence a house and describes sexual access as coming to them; BSB uses “palace” and “slept with them”.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says to escape “our eyes”; BSB leaves the eyes implicit.
The Hebrew separately says they went out behind him and went out from Jerusalem; BSB combines their departure.
The Hebrew says the sword fell out when he stepped forward; BSB makes Joab actively slip the dagger from the sheath.
The Hebrew makes Joab’s right hand the grammatical subject of seizing the beard; BSB makes Joab the subject.
The Hebrew says he did not repeat the blow and then Amasa died; BSB explains this as no need to repeat because he was dead.
The Hebrew leaves the man stood over unnamed; BSB supplies Amasa.
The Hebrew repeats seeing each passerby stop; BSB leaves that repeated observation implicit.
The Hebrew leaves the removed person unnamed; BSB supplies “Amasa’s body”.
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed; BSB supplies Sheba.
The Hebrew leaves the arriving besiegers and besieged man unnamed; BSB supplies “Joab’s troops” and “Sheba”.

The Hebrew emphatically repeats the root for asking; BSB specifies “counsel” and “disputes”.

The Hebrew explicitly names Joab as recipient of the woman’s reply; BSB leaves the addressee implicit.
The Hebrew leaves the dispersing group unnamed and says each went to his tents; BSB supplies “his men” and has “his own home”.
